practicePlans.title: 10-minute fielding practice

blocks.title: Shake-out warm-up
instructions: Jog in place 30 seconds.
Ten arm circles each direction.

blocks.title: Rolled ground balls (tennis ball)
instructions: Parent kneels 15 feet away and rolls a tennis ball.
Player fields in the triangle, funnels to the belly, flips it back.
blocks.parentTip: Roll to the glove side first; move it around only after six clean fielded balls.

blocks.title: Recap
instructions: Ask: what was the best thing you did today?

practicePlans.funChallenge: Ten clean grabs in a row earns the player the right to pick dinner.
practicePlans.recap: Talk about one cue to remember.

practicePlans.title: Comets practice: ground balls and throwing

blocks.title: Dynamic warm-up and throwing progression
instructions: Two laps, then high knees, butt kicks and arm circles.
Partners 20 feet apart, five easy throws, then back up to 40 and 60 feet.
Finish with ten throws at a target on the chest.
safety: No long toss until arms are loose.

blocks.title: Station 1 · Ready Position Freeze Game
instructions: Call 'Pitcher's ready!' Every player hops into the ready position: feet wider than the shoulders, knees bent, bottom down, hands out in front with palms facing the caller.
Count out loud to three while they freeze. Walk around and check gently: feet wider than shoulders, weight on the balls of the feet, hands floating in front of the knees instead of resting on them.
Call 'Relax!' and let everyone stand tall and shake out their legs for a few seconds.
cues: Weight on your toes, not your heels
blocks.setup: Players spread out at arm's length from each other, all facing the parent or coach who will do the calling. No ball is needed.
blocks.groups: Six players with the head coach
blocks.reps: 8 to 10 freezes with a 5-second shake-out between each

blocks.title: Station 2 · Shadow Circles and Towel Snaps
instructions: Shadow circles with no towel: hand out of the glove thumb down past the back pocket, up to the L with the elbow level with the shoulder, freeze two seconds, then through to the opposite hip. Ten slow reps.
Partner checks the L from the side: elbow at shoulder height, fingers on top, ball-hand above the head.
Pick up the towel. Step with the glove-side foot and make the same circle, snapping the towel so it slaps the partner's hand at the finish.
cues: Thumb down out of the glove
blocks.setup: Player stands sideways to an imaginary target with a hand towel held by one corner in the throwing hand. A partner holds an open hand or glove at chest height, one long stride plus an arm's length in front of the player's front foot.
blocks.reps: 10 slow shadow circles, then 2 sets of 10 towel snaps

blocks.title: Infield rhythm: field it, funnel, throw to first
instructions: Full infield, coach hits ground balls from home.
Every ball is fielded and thrown to first; first baseman rotates every five throws.
Outfielders back up every throw.

blocks.title: Game · Knocking-Knuckle Line-Up
instructions: On 'pick it up', each player bends down and picks up the bat with both hands, bottom hand nearest the knob.
Players lift the bat to shoulder height and look down the handle. The knocking knuckles of both hands should make a rough line, and the hands should touch.

blocks.title: Wrap-up and home assignment
instructions: One thing each player did well today.
Home practice this week: ten rolled ground balls a day.

safety: Helmets on for every live ball.
practicePlans.recap: Ground balls looked cleaner by the end; keep the glove out front at home this week.

instructions: Players move the tee to inside, middle, and outside positions and learn that the contact point changes with each one. A small load (a slight shift of weight back before the swing) and keeping the hands inside the ball give the swing power without a long loop.
cues: Put a cone where each tee location's ball should land and let the cones, not you, tell the hitter where contact happened.

instructions: Tagging up means a runner waits on the base until a fly ball is caught, then runs. Players learn the rule from the runner's side and the fielder's side: drop steps and angles to the ball, and calling it three times so two fielders never collide.
cues: Put a runner on third during every fly-ball drill so fielders learn to catch and throw in one motion while the runner practices the tag.

about: DVYAA has served families across the Delaware Valley since 1961. We are run entirely by volunteers and chartered by Little League International.
Every child plays. Every team practices the same fundamentals. Every family gets the GamePlanIQ Academy so you can practice at home even if you never played.

faq.a: Children who live or attend school inside our league boundary and meet the league age for a division. League age is set each season from the official Little League age chart; we confirm eligibility with residence or school documents during registration.
Fees range by division and include a jersey, hat and insurance. A 15% family discount applies to each additional child, and financial assistance is available with no paperwork beyond a short request.

faq.q: What equipment does my child need?
faq.a: A glove that fits and comfortable athletic shoes. The league provides helmets, catcher's gear and team bats, though many families bring their own. Bats must carry the USA Baseball stamp.
Field decisions are posted on the Field Status page and sent as a notification by 3:00 PM on weekdays and 7:00 AM on weekends.
We ask every family for two volunteer hours a season: concessions, field prep, scorekeeping or team parent. Sign up in the app.

policies.title: Code of Conduct
policies.body: Players, parents, coaches and umpires treat each other with respect. No arguing balls and strikes. One warning, then removal from the complex.

policies.title: Safety Plan
policies.body: Our ASAP safety plan covers first aid kits at every field, lightning policy, heat guidelines and background checks for every volunteer who works with children.

policies.title: Refund Policy
policies.body: Full refund before the first practice, 50% before the first game, no refunds after. Exceptions for injury or relocation.

sections.officer: Our safety officer is the board member listed under Board & contact. Coaches reach them by phone on game days; the league president covers when they are unavailable.
sections.distribution: The plan is posted in GamePlanIQ under Documents & policies and reviewed in the preseason coaches meeting. Completion of the Coach certification modules records that each volunteer read the safety material.
sections.emergency: Each field's address and entrance is listed in Fields & weather. In an emergency one adult stays with the injured player, one calls 911 and gives the address, one meets the ambulance and one gathers the team.
sections.screening: Every adult with repetitive access to players completes a background check through the league's authorized provider before the season. Only the status and expiry are recorded, in Volunteers.
sections.training: Coaches complete the Coach certification modules (abuse awareness, concussion, first aid and emergency plan, pitch counts and arm care, heat and lightning) and attend the preseason fundamentals clinic.
sections.inspection: The home team's manager walks the field before every game and practice and reports hazards to the safety officer. Helmets, bats and catcher's gear are inspected at the first practice and monthly after that.
sections.concessions: Concession volunteers wash hands on arrival, keep hot foods hot and cold foods cold, and know where the fire extinguisher is. The stand is inspected at the start of each season.
sections.firstaid: A first aid kit is kept at every field and in every team bag. The safety officer checks field kits monthly using the kit checklist in GamePlanIQ and restocks from the league supply.
sections.reporting: Any injury, behavior or facility incident is reported in GamePlanIQ the same day by the adult who saw it. The safety officer reviews within 48 hours, follows up with the family, and files insurance paperwork when care was needed.
